provenance.source_study_name: Eurasian griffon vulture in France (Grands Causses 2018) ID_PROG 961

descriptive_sensor_agreement.qualifier: The barometric channel may be GPS- or pressure-model-calibrated, so the two native columns are NOT independent replications of biological individual effects; day-by-day centered values differ substantially even with high correlations.

evidence_boundary.supported: In a separately archived, differently named wild Gyps fulvus tracking study, different native height observation columns show the same heldout bird-ID-associated distribution-shape pattern within matched 5km source GPS cells/days.
not_supported: Independent height sensor causality or individual differences not linked to GPS tag/error: both height series can share calibrations, body-mounted location and device-specific errors.
Same 27 birds are 54 independent biological replications: both channels score exactly the same bird-days and target fixes.
Regional thermal/wind controls or bird-specific atmospheric response was tested: source D1 merely tests bird-ID height-shape identity.
True altitude above terrain was measured: native GPS height-above-msl and barometric height have distinct geodesy/mapping requirements.
Exact numeric parent Movebank study and all biological bird identity equivalence were independently established across old source archivals.
Positive p proves evolutionary adaptation, individual specialization in resource partitioning, or universal aeroecological rule.
evidence_boundary.next: Freeze and test independent regional CERRA 100m wind time-state donor support for the same original 28 birds using only source GPS time/XY, then treat any within-source wind-context experiment as POST-OUTCOME exploratory because the original height-D1 response has already been inspected.
